transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2027-09-01
- Time: 14:00 UTC
- Duration: 45 minutes
- Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Julia Park (Lakeside Head of ML), Ethan Morales (CTO), Priya Singh (Infra), Ben Ortiz (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Quick renewal check, interest in going from hosted to dedicated in us-west and adding APAC region; run benchmarks before committing to new capacity; legal review for extension.

[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, and then let's jump into where Lakeside is on usage and renewals.
[00:12] Julia Park: Hi, Julia here. Quick note, our Q3 spike was higher than predicted, so the current hosted plan is getting pinched, latency up especially in west pacific, like APAC, sorry, pacific region.
[00:25] Ethan Morales: Ethan as well, yeah we saw tail latency at peak, and we want to avoid that for the loan decisioning flows.
[00:33] Marcus Lee: Yeah, understood. For those spikes, dedicated capacity or a region add will help — we generally see 30-60% improvement in p95 when isolating pools and pre-warming KV cache.
[00:47] Priya Singh: Quick question — when you say KV cache, that's the key-value cache, right? sometimes internal docs call it KV cash, so just making sure.
[00:55] Marcus Lee: Yes KV cache, sorry transcription sometimes flips it.
[01:02] Ben Ortiz: From procurement perspective, timeline matters. We're aiming to lock terms before 10/1 if possible.
[01:10] Avery Chen: Good, that aligns. Today we want to discuss two asks: one, dedicated capacity bump to support peak traffic (roughly 2x current committed GPUs) and two, adding APAC region with a small reserved pool and burst capacity.
[01:24] Julia Park: Correct. Also need to confirm data residency and key management — we need KMS integration and audit logs for all inference requests.
[01:33] Marcus Lee: We support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations on Private, and for Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS for encryption at rest and envelope encryption. Audit logs are available via the Console with token-level tracing.
[01:47] Ethan Morales: Is the audit log retention configurable? We may need 1 year retention for compliance.
[01:53] Priya Nair: Yes, retention tiers are an add-on, we'll include options in the pricing sheet.
[01:59] Julia Park: Also curious about canary rollback / graceful degradation if APAC region becomes degraded. We can't afford to have the decisioning pipeline fall back to a slower model for a period without notice.
[02:11] Marcus Lee: We have routing policies — latency-first routing with automatic fallback to a compatibility model in another region. We can set strict SLOs and have alerts; we'll show you the routing policy config in the benchmark.
[02:24] Ben Ortiz: On pricing, curious about committed vs on-demand. If we commit to dedicated for 12 months vs 36 months, what are typical discounts?
[02:33] Avery Chen: We have a sliding discount scale. I'll send a worksheet with three scenarios: 12-month reserved, 24-month, and 36-month with higher discounts and included burst credits.
[02:45] Julia Park: For the APAC add, we need to test model performance with our inference pipeline — we have custom tokenization and post-processing steps that add latency. Can we run an APAC benchmark with our containerized post-processing?
[02:57] Marcus Lee: Yes — we'll do a benchmark run that uses your postproc container and traffic profile. We typically run a 2-hour ramp plus peak simulation. Will need credentials and an infra contact.
[03:10] Priya Singh: That's me, I'll provide topology diagrams and a service account.
[03:15] Marcus Lee: Great. I'll scope the benchmark and send the checklist.
[03:19] (short pause, background noise)
[03:30] Julia Park: Also SOC 2 — are we covered? Our security team will want written evidence of controls for the Dedicated deployment.
[03:38] Priya Nair: Redwood Dedicated is SOC 2 Type II compliant; we'll send the audit summary and a control matrix. For Private deployments we can provide more documentation.
[03:47] Ethan Morales: Any blockers for VPC peering? We need VPC/VPN options for the private control plane.
[03:54] Marcus Lee: We have VPC peering and private link options; for on-prem there's an additional packaging step. For dedicated we do region-based VPC configurations.
[04:05] Ben Ortiz: On legal, we'll need to compare liability and data handling clauses for the renewed T&Cs. I'll loop in legal once pricing is in place.
[04:14] Avery Chen: Perfect. Proposed timeline: send pricing + audit docs by 9/3, run benchmarks week of 9/6, review benchmark results 9/10, settle terms mid-September and aim for contract signature before 10/1. Does that sound right?
[04:28] Julia Park: Sounds good. One more technical question — quantization/throughput tradeoffs. In our tests, lower precision models saved cost but increased hallucination risk. How do you recommend we evaluate quality vs cost?
[04:40] Marcus Lee: We'll include eval runs alongside throughput tests — keep a hold-out set of prompts and measure regression on quality metrics; Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization profiles by workload. We'll log metrics so you can decide.
[04:53] Priya Singh: For the APAC placement, are there any extra costs for dedicated GPUs in that region? We expect prices to be a bit higher.
[04:59] Avery Chen: There can be a regional delta; I'll flag estimated region premiums in the pricing worksheet.
[05:06] Julia Park: Great. Any competitive concerns? We evaluated Anthropic for safety but their latency profile didn't meet our SLOs in our tests.
[05:15] Marcus Lee: Understood. We'll make sure the benchmark mirrors your worst-case traffic to validate.
[05:22] Ben Ortiz: Procurement question — do you accept PO and do you have standard enterprise invoicing options?
[05:28] Priya Nair: Yes, we accept PO, net-30 or net-45 can be discussed depending on contract length; we'll include invoicing terms in the term sheet.
[05:36] (crosstalk)
[05:45] Marcus Lee: Quick technical: for caching and batching, we recommend a prefix cache warm-up before peak windows, and continuous batching tuned to your seq length distribution — please share seq length histogram.
[05:58] Julia Park: I'll export those stats by 9/7.
[06:03] Avery Chen: Closing recap — action items: Marcus to scope benchmarks, Avery to send pricing and audit docs, Julia to share traffic/seq stats, Ben to prepare procurement/PO path. Meet again after benchmark results.
[06:18] Ethan Morales: One last note — if the benchmark shows we're good, we'll likely move to 24-month reserved capacity and start the legal cadence.
[06:27] Avery Chen: Great, we'll aim for that. Thanks everyone.

-- End Transcript --

Notes on transcription: occasional word swaps (KV cash / cache), speaker labels are accurate except short section where background noise obscured speaker and was labeled generically.
